# Golden M0 corpus — narinfo/NAR regression fixtures

Byte-exact captures of what bunkerd serves for one seeded cache,
created for the artifact-serving program's M0 baseline (design:
`~/workspace/bunker-artifact-serving/DESIGN.md` §8). The prime
directive of that program is *zero change to Nix protocol
behaviour*; this corpus is how later milestones prove it.

## Layout

- `regenerate.sh` — rebuilds the corpus from scratch (throwaway
  bunkerd, seeded cache, real uploads) and either verifies it
  against `expected/` (default) or rewrites `expected/` (`write`).
- `config.toml.template` — the fixture server's configuration.
  Chunking (64 KiB threshold, 16/64/256 KiB FastCDC) and compression
  (zstd) are pinned to the production template defaults so the
  corpus stays stable even if defaults change later.
- `seed/content-a/` — path A's content (a small directory tree).
  Path B's content is generated by the script (600,000
  deterministic pseudo-random bytes + a note), so it is not
  committed.
- `expected/` — the captured bytes:
  - `nix-cache-info.txt` — body of `GET /golden-m0/nix-cache-info`
  - `<hash>.narinfo` — body of `GET /golden-m0/<hash>.narinfo`
    for each fixture path
  - `<hash>.nar` — body of `GET /golden-m0/nar/<hash>.nar`
  - `chunk-counts.txt` — `num_chunks` per store path, read from
    the seeded database after upload
  - `SHA256SUMS` — checksums of the above

## Fixture paths

As produced by the first `write` run (2026-10-13, primo):

- Path A: `/nix/store/0251v6dlj190y3hlqrrv4mshr4h6f1sy-golden-a`
  — small tree; NAR is 896 bytes, below the chunking threshold,
  stored as **1 chunk**; the served (zstd) `.nar` is 292 bytes.
  Its narinfo carries an empty `References:` line.
- Path B: `/nix/store/hch7h8q23yrf21z7zbsc2rp07riac55b-golden-b`
  — 600,000 incompressible bytes; NAR is 600,536 bytes, stored as
  **10 chunks**; the served `.nar` is 600,626 bytes. It lists path
  A in its `References` and carries a `Deriver` label
  (`golden-b.drv`, a fixture label — the server stores and
  re-emits it verbatim) so the optional narinfo fields are
  exercised.

Neither narinfo carries `FileHash`/`FileSize`: Bunker stores NARs
as chunks, so there is no single compressed file to hash (the
fields are absent by design — see `NarInfo` in
`server/src/narinfo/mod.rs`). The corpus pins that behaviour too.

## Determinism

- The cache `golden-m0` is created with a **fixed, test-only
  keypair** (in `regenerate.sh`; seed = SHA-256 of
  "bunker golden-m0 fixture keypair (test only)"). Ed25519
  signatures are deterministic, so the narinfo `Sig:` lines are
  byte-stable. Never use this key outside this fixture.
- The JWT signing key in the config template is the test key
  already published in `server/src/config.rs` tests
  (`TEST_TOKEN_ED25519_SECRET_BASE64`). Test-only.
- Store paths are content-addressed (`nix-store --add` against the
  host's real Nix store — the script adds the two fixture paths to
  it; they are inert data). NARs come from `nix-store --dump`.
- One caveat: the served `.nar` bytes are the zstd-compressed
  stream the server stored. zstd output is deterministic for a
  given encoder version and settings; re-verify on the same
  machine class (primo) the corpus was written on. If a future
  zstd upgrade ever changes those bytes legitimately, the diff
  will show it here first — that is the corpus doing its job, and
  the bump must be reviewed, not rubber-stamped.

## Re-verifying (later milestones)

Build the server under test, then:

```sh
cargo build -p bunker-server
server/tests/fixtures/golden-m0/regenerate.sh verify
```

`verify` exits non-zero and prints a `diff -r` if any served byte
changed. `BUNKERD`/`BUNKERADM` env vars point the script at other
builds (e.g. `target/release/bunkerd`).

There is deliberately no `cargo test` wrapper: the server crate
has no HTTP integration harness to hang one on, and the script is
the replay procedure the design's test plan calls for.
